- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated overshoot; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or 2.0x if sentiment remains high.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion: subtract 0.2–0.4x the spike magnitude from forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 10+ consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore trend; apply downward bias of 0.1–0.3 to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67/0.33 alternation), model overfits to recent sentiment; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00), model often underestimates; add 0.1–0.2 to forecast to account for risk aversion or market panic.
